questions.question: Which of the following amendment acts included Fundamental Duties in the Constitution of India?
questions.solution:
The 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 is the landmark legislation that included Fundamental Duties in the Constitution of India. It added a new part, Part IV-A, consisting of only one article, Article 51A.

Note: This amendment is often referred to as the 'Mini-Constitution' due to the large number of changes it introduced during the Emergency period.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding composition of the State Legislative Council?

A. The maximum strength of the Council is fixed at one-third of the total strength of the Assembly.

B. The minimum strength of the Council is fixed at 40.

C. A total of 5/6 of the total number of members of a Legislative Council are indirectly elected and 1/6 members are nominated.

D. The nominations (nominated members) made by the Governor can be challenged in the court.
questions.solution: Statements A, B, and C only are correct. Regarding the State Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad): (A) The maximum strength is 1/3rd of the Assembly, (B) the minimum is 40, and (C) 5/6 members are indirectly elected while 1/6 are nominated by the Governor. Statement D is incorrect because the Governor's nominations (from fields like literature, science, art, etc.) are generally not subject to challenge in court regarding the merit of the person's 'special knowledge'.

questions.question: Which part of the Constitution of India incorporates the Directive Principles of State Policy?
questions.solution:
Part IV of the Indian Constitution (Articles 36 to 51) incorporates the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP). These principles are non-justiciable in nature but are fundamental in the governance of the country.

Additional Info: They aim to establish a social and economic democracy and a welfare state.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding removal of the President of India?
A. The impeachment process can be initiated in the either House of Parliament.
B. The impeachment charges must be signed by the one-third members of the House in which the process is initiated.
C. In the impeachment process, a 30 days’ notice should be given to the President.
D. The impeachment resolution is passed by a majority of two-thirds of the total membership of that House.
questions.solution: Statements A and D only are correct. (A) The impeachment can be initiated in either House. (D) The resolution must be passed by a two-thirds majority of the total membership of each House. Statement B is incorrect because the charges must be signed by 1/4th (not 1/3rd) of the members. Statement C is incorrect because a 14 days’ (not 30 days) notice is required.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a Fundamental Right mentioned in the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution: The Right to vote is a Constitutional/Legal Right, but it is NOT a Fundamental Right under Part III. Fundamental Rights like the Right to Equality (Art 14-18), Right to Freedom (Art 19-22), and Right to Freedom of Religion (Art 25-28) are basic human rights protected by the Constitution and are enforceable by the judiciary.

questions.question: As per Article 172(2) ____________ of a State shall NOT be subject to dissolution.
questions.solution:
According to Article 172(2), the Legislative Council of a State (where it exists) is a permanent body and shall NOT be subject to dissolution. However, one-third of its members retire every second year.

Note: This is similar to the Rajya Sabha (Council of States) at the central level.

questions.question: The Indian Constitution was enacted on which of the following dates?
questions.solution: The Indian Constitution was enacted and adopted on 26th November 1949. This day is now celebrated annually as Constitution Day (Samvidhan Divas). While many provisions came into force on this day, the Constitution officially commenced in its entirety on 26th January 1950.

questions.question: Who administers oath of office to the Vice President of India?
questions.solution:
The President of India (or someone appointed by them) administers the oath of office to the Vice President. According to Article 69, the Vice President swears to bear true faith and allegiance to the Constitution of India.

Note: The President’s oath is administered by the Chief Justice of India.

questions.question: Which of the following committees recommended for the inclusion of fundamental duties in the Constitution of India?
questions.solution:
The Swaran Singh Committee, set up in 1976, recommended the inclusion of Fundamental Duties. The committee believed that citizens should be aware that while they enjoy rights, they also have duties toward the nation.

Related Info: The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee is associated with Panchayati Raj.

questions.question: Who among the following was the first Chief Election Commissioner of India?
questions.solution:
Sukumar Sen was the first Chief Election Commissioner of India, serving from 1950 to 1958. He successfully managed the first two general elections of independent India (1951-52 and 1957).

Fact: He also served as the first Chief Election Commissioner for Sudan.

questions.question:
Assume a situation where A has gone to a cinema hall with her friends to watch a movie. In the next seat she realises that it is her maid who is also watching the movie. Now A asks her maid to leave the cinema hall.
In the above scenario, which of the following Article of the Constitution of India can provide relief to the maid?
questions.solution: Article 15 of the Constitution prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth. It specifically states that no citizen shall be subject to any disability or restriction regarding access to public places (like cinema halls, shops, or restaurants). Thus, the maid can seek relief under Article 15.

questions.question: The concept of fundamental rights first came into being in the Magna Carta in ________.
questions.solution:
The concept of fundamental rights originated in the Magna Carta (The Great Charter) in England in 1215. It was a document signed by King John which, for the first time, established that everyone, including the king, was subject to the law.

Note: It is often called the 'Mother of All Constitutions'.

questions.question: In case an Indian citizen is arrested and denied the right to be defended, then in such a situation, which Article of the Indian Constitution can provide a relief?
questions.solution:
Article 22 provides protection against arrest and detention in certain cases. It guarantees the right of every arrested person to be informed of the grounds of arrest and the right to consult and be defended by a legal practitioner of their choice.

Note: It also mandates that the person be produced before a magistrate within 24 hours.

questions.question: The Chairman of a State Public Service Commission can be removed by the order of the ____________.
questions.solution:
The Chairman of a State Public Service Commission (SPSC) can only be removed by the President, even though they are appointed by the Governor. The removal can happen on grounds of misbehaviour after an inquiry by the Supreme Court, or due to insolvency or infirmity of mind/body.

Key Distinction: Appointment by Governor, Removal by President.

questions.question: Which of the following Amendment Acts added four new subjects (Article 39, 39A, 43A, 48A) in the Directive Principles of State Policy?
questions.solution: The 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 added four new Directive Principles: Article 39 (Opportunities for healthy development of children), Article 39A (Equal justice and free legal aid), Article 43A (Participation of workers in management), and Article 48A (Protection of environment).

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding the Finance Commission of India?
A. The Finance Commission consist of a Chairman and four other members.
B. The recommendations made by the Finance Commission are binding on the government and government needs to grant funds according to the advice of the Commission.
C. Article 280 of the Indian Constitution talks about the recommendations of the Finance Commission.
questions.solution: Statement A only is correct. The Finance Commission consists of a Chairman and 4 members (A). Statement B is incorrect because its recommendations are advisory and not binding on the government. Statement C is incorrect because Article 280 establishes the Commission; the recommendations themselves are laid before Parliament under Article 281.

questions.question: What is the significance of 26 January being chosen as a day to celebrate the Republic Day, aside from the adoption of the constitution?
questions.option_1: Foundation day of the Indian National Congress
questions.solution: The date 26 January was chosen for Republic Day because on this day in 1930, the Indian National Congress declared Purna Swaraj (Complete Independence) at the Lahore Session. To honor this historic milestone, the Constitution was commenced on the same date in 1950.

questions.question: The finance commission of India is required to make recommendations to the ___________.
questions.solution:
The Finance Commission is a quasi-judicial body constituted every five years to make recommendations to the President of India. The President then causes these recommendations to be laid before each House of Parliament.

Function: It primarily deals with the distribution of tax proceeds between the Union and the States.

questions.question: Which of the following parts of the Indian Constitution deals with fundamental rights?
questions.solution: Part III (Articles 12 to 35) of the Indian Constitution deals with Fundamental Rights. These rights are known as the Magna Carta of India because they protect the liberties and freedoms of citizens against the arbitrary exercise of state power.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution empowers the Supreme Court to review its own judgements or orders?
questions.solution: Article 137 empowers the Supreme Court to review its own judgements or orders. This is essential because the Supreme Court is the final court of appeal, and this power allows it to correct any errors or 'miscarriage of justice' that might have occurred in previous rulings.

questions.question: ________of the Constitution of India says that the State shall take steps to organise panchayats and endow them with such powers and authority as may be necessary to enable them to function as units of self-government.
questions.solution: Article 40 (a Directive Principle) states that the State shall organise village panchayats and give them necessary powers to function as units of self-government. This vision was later given constitutional status through the 73rd Amendment Act, 1992.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution deals with the Right against Exploitation?
questions.solution:
Article 23 (and Article 24) deals with the Right against Exploitation. Article 23 specifically prohibits human trafficking, 'begar' (forced labor), and other similar forms of forced labor.

Note: Article 24 prohibits the employment of children below 14 years in factories or hazardous conditions.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution empowers the Parliament to establish additional courts for better administration of laws made by it?
questions.solution: Article 247 empowers Parliament to provide for the establishment of additional courts for the better administration of laws made by Parliament or of any existing laws with respect to a matter enumerated in the Union List.

questions.question: Which of the following rights is guaranteed by Article 25 of the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
Article 25 guarantees the Right to Freedom of Religion. It includes the freedom of conscience and the right to freely profess, practice, and propagate religion.

Scope: This right is available to all persons (citizens and non-citizens) but is subject to public order, morality, and health.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution stipulates that the law declared by the Supreme Court shall be binding on all courts within the territory of India?
questions.solution: Article 141 of the Indian Constitution stipulates that the law declared by the Supreme Court shall be binding on all courts within the territory of India. This ensures uniformity and consistency in the judicial system across the country.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India enshrines to value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture?
questions.solution:
Article 51(A), which lists the Fundamental Duties, includes the duty to 'value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture' under clause (f).

Clarification: Article 48A is a DPSP about the environment, and Article 43A is about workers' participation in management.
